cases.purpose: attach control gives the controller role (status controller=1); a second control attach is rejected with EBUSY and does not change the counts; an observer can still attach next to the controller and is counted separately.
cases.script:
root=$HOME/br
/usr/bin/mkdir -m 700 "$root" || exit 125
exec 8<>fifo
sent=''
field() { local s=$1 k=$2; [[ $s =~ (^| )$k=([0-9-]+) ]] && printf '%s' "${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"; }
cleanup() {
  local st bp i
  st=$(ptybroker status "$root" s 2>/dev/null); bp=$(field "$st" broker_pid)
  ptybroker terminate "$root" s >/dev/null 2>&1
  [[ -n $sent ]] && kill $sent 2>/dev/null
  if [[ -n $bp ]]; then for ((i=0; i<100; i++)); do [[ -d /proc/$bp ]] || break; read -t 0.05 -u 8 x; done; fi
}
trap cleanup EXIT
ptybroker create "$root" s -- /usr/bin/cat >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "create=$?" > rc
ptybroker attach "$root" s control h1 2>e-c1; echo "control1=$?" >> rc
st=$(ptybroker status "$root" s); echo "after-c1 controller=$(field "$st" controller) observers=$(field "$st" observers)" > roles
ptybroker attach "$root" s control h2 2>e-c2; echo "control2=$?" >> rc
[[ $(<e-c2) == *"Device or resource busy"* ]] && echo busy > c2-diag || echo "other:$(<e-c2)" > c2-diag
st=$(ptybroker status "$root" s); echo "after-c2 controller=$(field "$st" controller) observers=$(field "$st" observers)" >> roles
ptybroker attach "$root" s observe o1 2>e-o1; echo "observe-with-controller=$?" >> rc
st=$(ptybroker status "$root" s); echo "after-o1 controller=$(field "$st" controller) observers=$(field "$st" observers)" >> roles

expected_files.roles:
after-c1 controller=1 observers=0
after-c2 controller=1 observers=0
after-o1 controller=1 observers=1

cases.purpose: Eight observers attach (documented limit); the ninth is rejected with EBUSY; all eight receive the bytes the child echoes; observers do not occupy the controller slot, so a controller can still attach.
cases.script:
root=$HOME/br
/usr/bin/mkdir -m 700 "$root" || exit 125
exec 8<>fifo
sent=''
field() { local s=$1 k=$2; [[ $s =~ (^| )$k=([0-9-]+) ]] && printf '%s' "${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"; }
cleanup() {
  local st bp i
  st=$(ptybroker status "$root" s 2>/dev/null); bp=$(field "$st" broker_pid)
  ptybroker terminate "$root" s >/dev/null 2>&1
  [[ -n $sent ]] && kill $sent 2>/dev/null
  if [[ -n $bp ]]; then for ((i=0; i<100; i++)); do [[ -d /proc/$bp ]] || break; read -t 0.05 -u 8 x; done; fi
}
trap cleanup EXIT
ptybroker create "$root" s -- /usr/bin/cat >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "create=$?" > rc
for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8; do
  ptybroker attach "$root" s observe "o$i" 2>"e-o$i"; echo "observer$i=$?" >> rc
done
ptybroker attach "$root" s observe o9 2>e-o9; echo "observer9=$?" >> rc
[[ $(<e-o9) == *"Device or resource busy"* ]] && echo busy > o9-diag || echo "other:$(<e-o9)" > o9-diag
st=$(ptybroker status "$root" s); echo "observers=$(field "$st" observers) controller=$(field "$st" controller)" > roles
ptybroker send "$root" s $'ping-w8\n'; echo "send=$?" >> rc
n=0
for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8; do
  hv=o$i; h=${!hv}; got=0
  for k in 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8; do
    ev=''
    ptybroker receive "$h" 1 ev 2000 >>"obs$i.out" 2>/dev/null || break
    [[ $ev == output* ]] && grep_ok=1
    [[ $(< "obs$i.out") == *ping-w8* ]] && { got=1; break; }
  done
  (( got )) && n=$((n+1))
done
echo "observers-receiving=$n" >> roles
ptybroker attach "$root" s control hc 2>e-ctl; echo "control-after-observers=$?" >> rc

expected_files.rc:
create=0
observer1=0
observer2=0
observer3=0
observer4=0
observer5=0
observer6=0
observer7=0
observer8=0
observer9=1
send=0
control-after-observers=0

  if [[ -n $bp ]]; then for ((i=0; i<100; i++)); do [[ -d /proc/$bp ]] || break; read -t 0.05 -u 8 x; done; fi

ptybroker create "$root" s -- /usr/bin/sleep 30 >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "create=$?" > rc

ptybroker attach "$root" s control h1 2>/dev/null; echo "control1=$?" >> rc

cases.purpose: A handle used from a subshell (another process) is rejected for receive, detach and fd without disturbing the attachment; the owner can still use it (receive times out with 124); after detach the same handle is stale and every use is rejected; the foreign detach did not release the observer.
cases.script:
root=$HOME/br
/usr/bin/mkdir -m 700 "$root" || exit 125
exec 8<>fifo
sent=''
field() { local s=$1 k=$2; [[ $s =~ (^| )$k=([0-9-]+) ]] && printf '%s' "${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"; }
cleanup() {
  local st bp i
  st=$(ptybroker status "$root" s 2>/dev/null); bp=$(field "$st" broker_pid)
  ptybroker terminate "$root" s >/dev/null 2>&1
  [[ -n $sent ]] && kill $sent 2>/dev/null
  if [[ -n $bp ]]; then for ((i=0; i<100; i++)); do [[ -d /proc/$bp ]] || break; read -t 0.05 -u 8 x; done; fi
}
trap cleanup EXIT
ptybroker create "$root" s -- /usr/bin/sleep 30 >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "create=$?" > rc
ptybroker attach "$root" s control h1 2>/dev/null; echo "attach=$?" >> rc
ptybroker attach "$root" s observe o1 2>/dev/null; echo "attach-observe=$?" >> rc
( ptybroker receive "$o1" 1 ev 50 >/dev/null 2>sub-err; echo "subshell-receive=$?" > sub-rc
  ptybroker detach "$o1" 2>sub-det-err; echo "subshell-detach=$?" >> sub-rc
  ptybroker fd "$o1" fdvar 2>sub-fd-err; echo "subshell-fd=$?" >> sub-rc )
for k in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do ptybroker receive "$o1" 1 ev 50 >/dev/null 2>/dev/null; r=$?; [[ $r == 124 ]] && break; done; echo "owner-receive-drain=$r" >> rc
ptybroker detach "$h1" 2>/dev/null; echo "detach=$?" >> rc
ptybroker detach "$h1" 2>e-again; echo "detach-again=$?" >> rc
ptybroker receive "$h1" 1 ev 50 >/dev/null 2>e-recv; echo "receive-stale=$?" >> rc
ptybroker fd "$h1" fdv 2>e-fd; echo "fd-stale=$?" >> rc
for f in sub-err sub-det-err sub-fd-err e-again e-recv e-fd; do [[ -s $f ]] && echo "$f=diagnosed" >> diag || echo "$f=silent" >> diag; done
st=$(ptybroker status "$root" s); echo "controller=$(field "$st" controller) observers=$(field "$st" observers)" > roles

expected_files.rc:
create=0
attach=0
attach-observe=0
owner-receive-drain=124
detach=0
detach-again=1
receive-stale=1
fd-stale=1
expected_files.diag:
sub-err=diagnosed
sub-det-err=diagnosed
sub-fd-err=diagnosed
e-again=diagnosed
e-recv=diagnosed
e-fd=diagnosed

cases.purpose: terminate ends the session child and its descendants, including a grandchild in the same session and one that started its own session, and has already waited for them when it returns; an unrelated sentinel process started outside the broker survives; the session directory is removed.
cases.script:
root=$HOME/br
/usr/bin/mkdir -m 700 "$root" || exit 125
exec 8<>fifo
sent=''
field() { local s=$1 k=$2; [[ $s =~ (^| )$k=([0-9-]+) ]] && printf '%s' "${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"; }
cleanup() {
  local st bp i
  st=$(ptybroker status "$root" s 2>/dev/null); bp=$(field "$st" broker_pid)
  ptybroker terminate "$root" s >/dev/null 2>&1
  [[ -n $sent ]] && kill $sent 2>/dev/null
  if [[ -n $bp ]]; then for ((i=0; i<100; i++)); do [[ -d /proc/$bp ]] || break; read -t 0.05 -u 8 x; done; fi
}
trap cleanup EXIT
/usr/bin/sleep 61 & sent=$!
echo "$sent" > sentinel.pid
ptybroker create "$root" s -- "$BASH" --noprofile --norc ./child.sh >/dev/null 2>e-create; echo "create=$?" > rc
for ((i=0; i<100; i++)); do [[ -s ready && -s gc-sess.pid ]] && break; read -t 0.1 -u 8 x; done
st=$(ptybroker status "$root" s); cpid=$(field "$st" child_pid)
same=$(<gc-same.pid); sess=$(<gc-sess.pid)
for p in $cpid $same $sess $sent; do [[ -d /proc/$p ]] && echo "before $p alive" >> live || echo "before $p gone" >> live; done
echo "child=$([[ $cpid != "" && $cpid != 0 ]] && echo set)" > pids
[[ $cpid != $same && $same != $sess && $sess != $sent ]] && echo distinct >> pids
ptybroker terminate "$root" s 2>e-term; echo "terminate=$?" >> rc
[[ -d /proc/$cpid ]] && echo child-alive > after || echo child-gone > after
[[ -d /proc/$same ]] && echo same-session-grandchild-alive >> after || echo same-session-grandchild-gone >> after
[[ -d /proc/$sess ]] && echo own-session-grandchild-alive >> after || echo own-session-grandchild-gone >> after
[[ -d /proc/$sent ]] && echo sentinel-alive >> after || echo sentinel-gone >> after
[[ -e $root/s ]] && echo session-dir-present >> after || echo session-dir-removed >> after
kill $sent; wait $sent 2>/dev/null; sent=''

files.child.sh:
/usr/bin/sleep 62 &
echo $! > gc-same.pid
/usr/bin/setsid "$BASH" --noprofile --norc -c 'echo $$ > gc-sess.pid; exec /usr/bin/sleep 64' &
echo ready > ready
wait

No reference executable exists; contract cases. Liveness is read from /proc/PID immediately after terminate returns, with no wait, so it measures the acknowledgment ordering.
